14 In a large container in an oil refinery, three oils of different densities are mixed. No chemical
activity occurs.
The mixture consists of:
1200 kg of oil of density 1100 kg m–3
1500 kg of oil of density 860 kg m–3
4000 kg of oil of density 910 kg m–3.
What is the density of the mixture?
A
927 kg m–3
B
933 kg m–3
C
957 kg m–3
D
1045 kg m–3

hints: Notice you are given three masses in $\text{kg}$ and three different densities in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, so the three volumes are not equal.
Recall $\rho = m/V$, so each oil contributes volume $V = m/\rho$ and total density is total mass divided by total volume.
Calculate $1200/1100 + 1500/860 + 4000/910$ to get total $V$ in $\text{m}^3$, then divide $6700 \text{ kg}$ by that total.
walkthrough: Total mass is conserved with no chemical activity: $m = 1200 + 1500 + 4000 = 6700 \text{ kg}$.
Mixture density is defined by $\rho = m/V$, so find total volume from $V = m/\rho$ for each oil.
Divide: $\rho = 6700/7.231 = 927 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ with correct units. This is option A

A.explanation: Total mass $6700 \text{ kg}$ divided by total volume $7.23 \text{ m}^3$ gives about $927 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: This is the mass-weighted mean of the densities, but density must be total mass divided by total volume, not averaged by mass.

C.explanation: This value is too high because it does not correctly add the three separate $V = m/\rho$ volumes before dividing.

D.explanation: This value exceeds the largest oil density contribution and cannot result from mixing $860$ to $1100 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ oils.
